replies.How would you explain, step by step, how: First, write down the standard form of a quadratic: ax² + bx + c = 0. Then use the quadratic formula: x equals negative b plus or minus square root of b squared minus four ac, all over two a. Plug in your values and simplify. To find stationary points, take the derivative of f(x), call it f'(x). Set f'(x) equal to zero and solve for x. These x-values are where the slope is flat. Plug each back into the original function to get the corresponding y-value. That gives you the coordinates of the stationary points.
